messages:
Nina: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A about credits + quotas. Two quick scenarios: 1) org has $200 promotional credits and suddenly traffic spikes 4x for ~10 minutes. 2) customer on Dedicated but also calls hosted endpoints (hybrid). Which enforcement kicks in first and what should we tell customers to expect?

Omar: TL;DR: enforcement order is rate limits/concurrency -> capacity protections -> billing. Credits reduce invoice amounts but do not increase token/concurrency quotas. So spike->429s or queued requests even if credits remain.

Jules: For scenario 1: short spikes often absorbed by our graceburst layer (10-30s, config by plan). If spike is sustained beyond graceburst, gateway rate-limiter will start returning 429s. Credits won't prevent this. Suggest telling customers to request a planned spike uplift for predictable events.

Zoe: Scenario 2 (hybrid): Dedicated traffic runs on the reserved pool and won't hit hosted org rate caps. However if they call hosted endpoints (e.g., fallbacks or different models) those requests are subject to hosted caps and billing. Credits generally only apply to hosted invoice items; Dedicated reserved fees are billed per contract.

Ben: Ops note: we log an event when credits hit 25%/10%/0% remaining and emit billing alerts. We also push a "quota-warning" when projected consumption will exceed soft caps in the next 12h. Customers should see both in Console and via webhook (if enabled).

billing-bot: invoice/credits update: account 0xA12: promo_credits=200.00 USD, expires=2026-09-12T00:00:00Z

Jules: Console roadmap update: per-key soft caps + webhook alerts planned next month, hard caps + per-route enforcement following quarter. Initially soft caps will only warn, not block, so customers can opt-in to auto-block behavior.

Nina: Good to know. For support playbooks, can we standardize the message? Something like: "Credits reduce billing but do not increase limits. Plan planned spikes via support to avoid throttling." Any additions?

Zoe: Add note about model fallbacks: during capacity pressure we may route to cheaper compatible variants (with a notification header) rather than dropping requests immediately. If customers need strict model fidelity, they should be on Dedicated with pinned versions.

ProductCouncil: internal note: prioritizing console visibility for token burn and forecast by route after per-key GA. PMs will share timelines with sales/solutions next week.

Nina: Cool. Can someone drop a short FAQ blurb in the docs and ping #support?

Jules: Will do 642. I'll create a two-paragraph FAQ + one-pager for urgent spikes and paste to #support in ~30m.
